name: Vesihirvi
body:
VESIHIRVI
CR 7

This majestic moose has a thick green pelt with touches of blue. Above its glowing turquoise eyes spreads an amberlike crown of antlers.

XP 3,200
N Large magical beast
Init +9; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, scent; Perception +10

DEFENSE

AC 20, touch 15, flat-footed 14 (+5 Dex, +1 dodge, +5 natural, –1 size)
hp 85 (9d10+36)
Fort +10, Ref +11, Will +6
DR 5/magic; Resist cold 10

OFFENSE

Speed 60 ft., swim 40 ft.
Melee gore +14 (2d6+6), 2 hooves +12 (1d6+3)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 10 ft.
Special Attacks powerful charge (gore, 4d6+9), wave stomp
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 9th; concentration +12; save DCs are Wis-based):

Constant—endure elements, water walk

STATISTICS

Str 23, Dex 20, Con 19, Int 11, Wis 16, Cha 12
Base Atk +9; CMB +16; CMD 32
Feats Dodge, Improved Initiative, Improved Natural Attack (gore), Multiattack, Power Attack
Skills Acrobatics +10 (+22 when jumping), Perception +10, Sense Motive +8, Survival +8, Swim +19; Racial Modifiers +12 Acrobatics when jumping
Languages Common, Sylvan (can’t speak)
SQ amphibious, skipping hooves

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Skipping Hooves (Ex)

When a vesihirvi is moving while using water walk, that movement doesn’t provoke attacks of opportunity.

Wave Stomp (Su)

Once every 1d4 rounds as a standard action, a vesihirvi can stomp its front hooves down on the surface of a body water, such as a lake, sending out a crushing wave that deals 6d6 points of bludgeoning damage in a 30-foot cone (Fortitude DC 17 for half ). A creature that fails its save is pushed back 15 feet. If the pushed creature hits something solid, it stops and takes an additional 2d6 points of bludgeoning damage. If another creature was hit by the pushed creature that creature is also dealt 2d6 points of bludgeoning damage (DC 17 Reflex negates). If the wave hits a small water craft, such as a fishing boat, it’s pushed back 20 feet (DC 22 Profession (sailor) to avoid).

The save DC is Wisdom-based.

ECOLOGY

Environment cold or temperate lakes
Organization solitary
Treasure incidental (antlers and pelt)

A vesihirvi is a mythical moose that resides in and around lakes deep in the wilderness, where it feeds on fish and plant life. The vesihirvi can step upon the surface of the water as if it were ground and its wide hooves allow it to move at ease underwater. During the winter, it cracks ice with its antlers and hooves to move in and out of the water.

The vesihirvi is very territorial, so it’s quick to attack any intruders or send their boats crashing towards rocks with violent waves. People from nearby fishing villages often revere the vesihirvi as a sacred beast. They offer it fresh fish and berries sent upon the lake on small ornate rafts, hoping that the vesihirvi allows them to fish and hunt within its territory in peace. Some foolhardy outsiders might be tempted to hunt the vesihirvi for its antlers and pelt, desired for their magical properties, but most are bound for a watery grave.
